newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian c.bank sells HRK295 mln bills, same rates.
newsitem.headline: Croatian c.bank sells HRK295 mln bills, same rates.

text.p: Croatia's central bank sold 294.8 million kuna in 35- and 91-day liquidity bills at a weekly auction on Wednesday.
The issued rates were unchanged at 7.0 and 8.50 percent, respectively after a cut in each by 50 basis points last week.
The central bank accepted all bids for its two maturities. But volume was boosted threefold after a large portion of bills were extended upon expiry, an official told Reuters.
New issues have totalled between 100 and 150 million kuna a week in the past two months as commercial banks invested their excess liquidity.
Central bank bills are not freely traded, but they can be used as collateral for Lombard loans, granted at 9.5 percent.
Monday's mandatory reserve payment drained 3.34 billion kuna from the banking system, some 44 million more than a fortnight ago.
The reserve ratio is now 34.85 percent of total kuna deposits, regardless of term. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
